title: Stabilize Flaky Workers on the Master UI
description:
**SITUATION:**

The previously built Spark standalone cluster on `ds-spark-01`, `ds-spark-02`, and `ds-spark-03` is warmed up and is the environment for this lab. Last on-call reported that **Workers look flaky on the Master UI** — ALIVE counts jump around — so nobody trusts the dashboard enough to diagnose Spark applications properly.

You own this incident: open the Master UI, check whether Workers are actually functional, and take the actions needed to get the cluster stable again.

One note from the previous engineer: when they brought a flaky Worker back up, it **looked fine on the Master UI at first**, then **after a short while it showed down again**. They never finished the dig. So even after fixing the worker daemon issue, wait for a minute to check the status in the Master UI.

Read the Master UI as a claim, then verify on the nodes before you trust it.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Read the Master UI, then investigate on the Worker hosts until you know what is wrong.
2. Restore the cluster so the Master stays at **2 ALIVE** — not a fix that looks good for a minute and then falls over again.
3. Fill the **Investigation** tab in story order, then Submit.

hints: Master RPC is spark://ds-spark-01:7077 — that is the control plane. UI ports 8080/8081/8082 are separate.
ps on each worker host — is the Worker JVM missing?
If bring-up looks good on the Master UI then the Worker shows down again after ~30s, compare spark.worker.timeout on that Worker host to the Master.
After fix: 2 ALIVE and it stays that way; 2 cores, 1536 MB, 0 running apps.
Fill the Investigation tab — missing answers fail on Submit.
